title: State Tax Collections
scope: This ledger ranks states on Census QTAX 2026 Q1 total state tax collections, Census Annual Survey of State Government Tax Collections for FY 2023 (including the individual-income share), Census ASPEP 2023 state government full-time-equivalent employment, Census of Governments 2022 state-and-local revenue and expenditure, 2022 government-unit counts, and Census Annual Survey of Public Pensions 2025 cash and investments and membership. NASBO rainy-day funds and party-dominance files remain later views.
exclusions: Does not cover Massachusetts retirement boards (DL-05), the Massachusetts type-of-tax split (Massachusetts Tax Collections), or party-registration advice. NASBO rainy-day figures and party-dominance files are pending: decline those.
heritage: Formerly the State Finance overview, State Employees, Government Organizations, Party Dominance, Financial Transparency, and US Public Pensions
vintage_note: Rebuilt Aug 15, 2026 from Census QTAX 2026 q1t3.xlsx, Total Taxes, 2026 Q1. U.S. equals 393,072,675 thousand dollars. Later views compiled Aug 15, 2026 are stored under derived.secondary. Tableau companions compiled Aug 16, 2026 are stored under derived.secondary.

lead: State government tax collections were $393.07 billion in the first quarter of 2026, +5.7% from a year earlier, excluding D.C. (SRC-629-01). Massachusetts collected $11.62 billion, rank 8 of 50 (derived, SRC-629-01). State governments employed 4,441,091 full-time-equivalent workers in 2023; Massachusetts employed 105,348, rank 14 of 50 (derived, SRC-629-03). Individual income taxes were 47.8% of Massachusetts FY 2023 state tax collections, rank 5 of 44 (derived, SRC-629-04). State and local revenue was $115.53 billion in Massachusetts in 2022, rank 12 of 51 (derived, SRC-629-05). Public pension systems held $127.85 billion in cash and investments (derived, SRC-629-07). The 2022 Census of Governments counted 857 government units in Massachusetts (SRC-629-06). State governments employed 4,441,091 full-time-equivalent workers in 2023; Massachusetts employed 105,348, rank 14 of 50 (derived, SRC-629-03). Individual income taxes were 47.8% of Massachusetts FY 2023 state tax collections, rank 5 of 44 (derived, SRC-629-04). NASBO rainy-day figures remain pending.
